audits.title: Unfolding possible non-medically indicated caesarean sections in five high-volume urban maternity units in Tanzania: A criterion-based clinical audit (a PartoMa sub-study)
audits.standard: Evidence-based locally co-created guidelines; pre-defined localised audit criteria for CS indications
audits.setting: Five urban high-volume maternity units in Dar es Salaam

cycle1.period: 1 October 2021 to 31 August 2022 (three months per unit)
cycle1.result: CS rate 31% (2949/9364). 1061/2674 (40%) did not comply with audit criteria: one previous CS with no trial of labour (50%), reported prolonged labour without slow progress (23%), fetal distress with normal FHR (21%).

audits.other_findings: Main indications were previous CS (42%), prolonged labour (28%) and fetal distress (21%).
audits.citation: Hansen S, Kujabi ML, Maimburg R, Macha A, Maembe L, Kabanda I, et al.. Unfolding possible non-medically indicated caesarean sections in five high-volume urban maternity units in Tanzania: A criterion-based clinical audit (a PartoMa sub-study). . 2024. doi:10.22541/au.172147158.84885427/v1.

audits.title: Prolonged labour as a driver of the ”caesarean section pandemic”: A criterion-based audit of caesarean sections in the five highest volume maternity units in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
audits.standard: Audit criteria for prolonged labour as a caesarean section indication
audits.setting: Five highest volume urban maternity units, Dar es Salaam

cycle1.result: 243/456 (53.3%) caesareans for prolonged labour were in uncomplicated labour: no trial of labour 78/243 (32.1%), partograph action line not crossed 145/243 (59.7%), second stage under 1 hour 20/243 (8.2%).

audits.other_findings: Overall caesarean rate 32% (2949/9364); 746/1517 (47.9%) of first-time caesareans were for prolonged labour.
audits.citation: Kujabi ML, Housseine N, Hansen S, D’mello BS, Meyrowitsch D, Konradsen F, et al.. Prolonged labour as a driver of the ”caesarean section pandemic”: A criterion-based audit of caesarean sections in the five highest volume maternity units in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. . 2024. doi:10.22541/au.172189402.28931805/v1.

audits.title: Prolonged labour as indication for emergency caesarean section: a quality assurance analysis by criterion-based audit at two Tanzanian rural hospitals.

cycle1.result: Suboptimal management in most cases; labour not prolonged in 26%, membranes intact in 16%; 36% of genuine prolonged labour sectioned at full dilatation.

audits.other_findings: Vacuum extraction not considered; staff awareness of guidelines poor.
audits.citation: Maaløe N, Sorensen BL, Onesmo R, Secher NJ, Bygbjerg IC. Prolonged labour as indication for emergency caesarean section: a quality assurance analysis by criterion-based audit at two Tanzanian rural hospitals. BJOG. 2012;119(5):605-613. doi:10.1111/j.1471-0528.2012.03284.x. PMID: 22329559.

audits.title: Disclosing doubtful indications for emergency cesarean sections in rural hospitals in Tanzania: a retrospective criterion-based audit.
audits.standard: Evidence-based audit criteria for realistic best practice

cycle1.result: 26% of emergency sections on inappropriate indications and 38% unclear; in prolonged labour 36% had timely progress and/or intact membranes.

audits.other_findings: Fetal distress indication in 14%, with reassuring or undocumented fetal heart in 84%; nine sectioned for intrauterine death without trial of instrumental delivery.

audits.title: Criteria-based audit of caesarean section in a referral hospital in rural Tanzania.
audits.standard: Audit criteria for caesarean section based on literature and national/international guidelines

cycle1.result: Of 82 CS among women with severe maternal morbidity or death, 36 (44.0%) met criteria without delay, 20 (24.4%) had correct indication but significant delay, and 16 (19.5%) did not meet criteria.

audits.other_findings: CS was more often correctly indicated during office hours (60.0% vs 36.0%).
audits.citation: Heemelaar S, Nelissen E, Mdoe P, Kidanto H, van Roosmalen J, Stekelenburg J. Criteria-based audit of caesarean section in a referral hospital in rural Tanzania. Trop Med Int Health. 2016;21(4):525-534. doi:10.1111/tmi.12683. PMID: 26892610.

audits.title: Caesarean section audit to improve quality of care in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania.
audits.standard: Appropriateness of Caesarean section indications judged by local audit panel and external auditor
audits.setting: St. Francis Referral Hospital, Ifakara, rural referral hospital

cycle1.result: Unjustified Caesarean sections 34% (local panel) and 75% (external auditor).

audits.intervention: Introduction of a focused Caesarean section audit system with local panel and external auditor review.

cycle2.result: Unjustified Caesarean sections fell to 23% (p = 0.29) and 52% (p = 0.01) by local panel and external auditor respectively.

audits.other_findings: 403 of 1868 deliveries (21.6%) were Caesarean; CS rate did not change (20.2 to 21.7%) and median decision-to-delivery interval was 83 min.
audits.citation: Dekker L, Houtzager T, Kilume O, Horogo J, van Roosmalen J, Nyamtema AS. Caesarean section audit to improve quality of care in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania. BMC Pregnancy Childbirth. 2018;18(1):164. doi:10.1186/s12884-018-1814-1. PMID: 29764384.

audits.title: Timing of cesarean section for prolonged labor in urban Tanzania: A criterion-based audit.
audits.standard: Predefined criteria for prolonged labour at each stage/phase
audits.setting: 5 urban maternity units, Dar es Salaam

cycle1.result: In 243/456 (53.3%) caesareans with a written indication of prolonged labour, labour was not prolonged; 78/243 (32.1%) had no trial of labour and 145/243 (59.7%) had not crossed the partograph action line.

audits.other_findings: Overall caesarean rate 32% (2949/9364); 47.9% of first caesareans cited prolonged labour.
audits.citation: Kujabi ML, Housseine N, Kabanda I, Msumi R, Maembe L, Sangalala M, et al.. Timing of cesarean section for prolonged labor in urban Tanzania: A criterion-based audit. AJOG Glob Rep. 2024;4(4):100404. doi:10.1016/j.xagr.2024.100404. PMID: 39583576.

audits.title: Disclosing possible nonmedically indicated cesarean sections in 5 high-volume urban maternity units in Tanzania: a criterion-based clinical audit.
audits.standard: Evidence-based, locally co-created criteria for caesarean section indication
audits.setting: Five urban high-volume maternity units, Dar es Salaam

cycle1.result: 1061/2674 (39.7%) caesarean sections did not meet audit criteria at time of decision; caesarean rate 31.5% (2949/9364).

audits.other_findings: Main non-compliant reasons: one previous caesarean with no trial of labour (49.6%), reported prolonged labour without slow progress (22.9%), fetal distress with normal heart rate (19.9%).

Disclosing possible nonmedically indicated cesarean sections in 5 high-volume urban maternity units in Tanzania: a criterion-based clinical audit. audits.title: Caesarean section audit by peer review.
audits.standard: Peer review of whether each caesarean section was reasonable (four consultants and four registrars)

cycle1.result: At least one auditor disagreed with the decision in 24 (48%) cases; complete agreement in 6/18 (33%) elective and 20/32 (63%) emergency sections.

audits.other_findings: Fetal distress was the main emergency indication in 20 (63%), with fetal blood sampling in only four; decision to delivery interval 13 to 160 min (mean 50 min). Structured diagnostic criteria and daily on-call peer review were proposed.
audits.citation: Wareham V, Bain C, Cruickshank D. Caesarean section audit by peer review. Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol. 1993;48(1):9-14. doi:10.1016/0028-2243(93)90046-f. PMID: 8449267.
